LOCAL_OPTIONS.why: Report 1 gives two of its three options no real price at all and falls back on a Southern California market rate, while Report 2 prices every option, says what each price buys, names credentials, flags the e-collar disqualifier, the FULL class round, the no-food method mismatch and the no-private-training limitation — he can choose a different option from Report 2 and cannot from Report 1.

FOUR_WEEK_PLAN.why: Report 2 names one protocol with click timing, rep counts, session length in minutes, step-sized distance increases and an observable advance marker at the end of every week, whereas Report 1's weeks are generic bullets that never say how far, how many, or how he knows he's ready to progress.

DECISION.why: Both give a clear hybrid verdict up front, but Report 2 attaches a dollar figure, a named class, and an explicit flip rule — the red-flag list plus "Four consistent weeks with zero movement in his threshold distance" — so he can check the decision against reality later.

DENSITY.why: Both end with a consolidated next-moves block and Report 2 packs far more per line than its length suggests, but Report 1 is tighter overall and Report 2 carries an off-spec ten-item mistakes list, a dog-park-personality digression and repeated re-citation of the same distance principle that cost him reading time.

GROUNDING.why: Report 1 cites five sources it never opened and substitutes a Southern California national-style rate for a local price — exactly the fallback he reacted badly to — while Report 2 opened fifteen of sixteen sources and lands real local figures like the $2,400 and $4,200 D For Dogz packages that match the provider ledger.

OVERALL.why: Report 2 gives him priced, credentialled, blocker-flagged local options and a four-week plan with weekly advance thresholds he can actually measure, where Report 1 leaves him phoning three trainers for quotes and guessing when to move closer — the extra reading is a fair price for that.
